title: GPU release orchestration compatibility catalog
author: Marisol Vega
body:
Overview:
This document is a compatibility catalog and operational playbook for coordinating GPU-related releases across CI/CD, Terraform/IaC, cloud networking, and fleet allocation. It captures the supported matrix (kernel, driver, container runtime, node-image bundles, quantized-runtime variants), promotion gates, and a deterministic rollback/rollforward checklist to be used by release owners and oncall engineers.

Scope:
- Applies to all production GPU node images and runtime component changes (driver upgrades, kernel updates, containerd/cri, NVIDIA/ROCm runtime, and compiled quantized kernels).
- Includes guidance for self-hosted and cloud-provider burst pools, warm-pool semantics, and cross-account egress considerations.
- Does NOT cover tenant application changes or model-level quantization; those are handled by serving-runtime teams.

Why this exists:
- GPU fleets are heterogeneous; small driver/kernel mismatches can produce silent correctness regressions or performance cliffs.
- Past incidents were caused by simultaneous changes in host kernel + driver + userland (libnvidia) that passed unit tests but failed under synthetic inference traffic. This catalog reduces those surprises.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Image bundle: A tested combination of host kernel, OS patchlevel, GPU driver, container runtime, and operator sidecars used in a node image build.
- Compatibility tag: short string used in CI to label artifacts (example: kg5-520-ctr1-q2 where kg5 = kernel 5.x generic, 520 = driver major, ctr1 = container runtime v1, q2 = quantized-kernel-profile 2).
- Promotion stages: staging -> regional-canary -> global-canary -> general-availability

Compatibility matrix (human-readable table):
- Columns: kernel | driver-series | container-runtime | gpu-runtime | quant-profile | notes
- Example entries:
  - 5.15.0-64-generic | 520.61.x | containerd 1.6.18 | nvidia-container-runtime 3.8 | q-profile-v2 | Supported for 8GB and 16GB V100 pools
  - 6.1.0-rc | 535.54.x | containerd 1.7.x | nvidia-container-runtime 3.9 | q-profile-v3 | Experimental: only for canary in non-critical pools

Promotion gates (CI/CD + IaC checks):
1) Build-time gates:
   - All node-image artifacts must pass the Image QA matrix: kernel smoke, driver smoke, container runtime sanity, and a metadata signature check.
   - Terraform plan must pass policy-as-code assertions (egress rules, subnet tagging, ENI limits) and map to the expected placement constraints for affected pools.
2) Integration canary (staging):
   - Create ephemeral pool (label: canary-image-<tag>) in staging account. Run the synthetic inference harness for at least 2 hours covering short (<=64 tokens) and long tail (<=2048 tokens) sequences.
   - Telemetry assertions (pass if all true): request error-rate < 0.5% above baseline, p95 latency change < +12%, avg GPU utilization within +/- 8% of baseline.
3) Regional canary (small subset of production regional warm pools):
   - Deploy to one AZ per region with canary capacity <= 2% of regional steady-state. Monitor for 24–48 hours.
4) Global canary (multi-region phased rollout):
   - 10% of traffic across regions for 72 hours. Automated rollback triggers on SRE alerts (see alert list).
5) GA (full rollout):
   - Auto-promote after successful canary OR manual approval if mitigations are required.

CI job and IaC conventions (examples):
- Image tag policy: images must include compatibility tag and SHA. Example: redwood/gpu-node:kg5-520-ctr1-q2-20250115-sha256-abc123
- Terraform module version pin: modules/gpu-node: v2.4.1 -> bump rule requires: changelog entry + one successful canary run recorded in the release ticket.
- CI snippets (YAML):
  - image-smoke-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run driver smoke tests
        run: ./ci/driver-smoke.sh --image ${{ inputs.image }}

Automated checks and telemetry requirements:
- Telemetry sources: node-exporter/gpu-exporter, nvml exporter, pod-level traces (traced by redwood-trace), and inference-harness metrics.
- Required dashboards: per-image SLO dashboard, per-quant-profile regression dashboard, and a release health composite.
- Alert list (examples):
  - image-p95-latency-regression: trigger if p95 latency increases > 20% for 15m
  - image-error-rate-spike: trigger if request error rate > 1% above baseline for 5m
  - gpu-mem-leak-heuristic: trigger if average free GPU memory decreases > 30% over 30m across >25% of fleet
- All alerts must contain the image compatibility tag and the Terraform module version in the alert payload.

Rollout runbook (numbered checklist for oncall / release owner):
1) Preflight (T-72h):
   - Create release ticket and attach compatibility matrix, CI run IDs, and canary schedule.
   - Verify IaC module pins and review policy-as-code results.
   - Notify affected teams (Serving, SRE, Observability) via release channel.
2) Staging canary (T-48h):
   - Deploy staging image bundle to ephemeral staging pools. Run smoke + 2-hour synthetic traffic test.
   - Capture baseline and tag image as staging-ready.
3) Regional canary (T-24h):
   - Promote Terraform workspace to create regional canary nodes using the pinned module version.
   - Enable automated circulation of warm-pool seeds (warmup) with limited prewarmed sessions.
   - Monitor release dashboards for 24h. If any gate fails, run rollback.
4) Global canary (T+0):
   - Phased traffic shift as described in Promotion gates. If automated rollback triggers, execute rollback playbook.
5) GA and cleanup (T+72h):
   - Promote module and image to GA tag, update internal catalogs, and create post-release evaluation ticket.

Rollback checklist (fast-path):
- If alert satisfies rollback criteria, execute the following within 15 minutes:
  1) Set release channel to "incident-rollback" and page release owner.
  2) Use IaC to revert the image tag in the canary workspace to the previous GA image (example terraform apply -var image=redwood/gpu-node:kg5-519-ctr1-q2).
  3) Scale up previous GA instance group to absorb traffic (use fleet-sentry operator).
  4) Disable automated promotions and pause any ongoing canaries.
  5) Collect diagnostics: nvml logs, dmesg, kmsg, kernel oops, runtime container logs, and a heap of failed inference payloads. Attach to the rollback ticket.
  6) Notify legal/security if any PII or customer data was present in failed payloads.

Fast rollforward (post-fix):
- After patch approval and a successful staging smoke, perform a small regional canary, validate for 6 hours, and re-run global canary for 24 hours. Document divergence root cause and corrective commit.

Terraform/IaC module guidance and examples:
- Module versioning: follow semver. Any driver bump that changes ABI must be a minor version bump with explicit compat matrix in module README.
- Example module inputs table (text):
  - image_tag: (string) required - image to deploy
  - enable_gpu_isolation: (bool) default: true
  - warm_pool_size: (int) default: 0
  - canary_label: (string) optional - label used for canary pools
- Recommend lockfile: maintain module_lock.json in the release branch and commit. CI refuses promotion without lockfile present.

Network & cloud-account considerations:
- Egress tagging: new images that introduce additional remote telemetry endpoints must be enumerated and allowed explicitly in tenant egress policies.
- ENI / IP planning: driver upgrades can temporarily increase DHCP churn. Coordinate with cloud-accounts to reserve extra ENIs for the canary window (+10% in high-density AZs).
- Cross-account warm-pools: for bursting into partner cloud accounts, pre-approve module version and ensure remote-state access tokens are scoped to canary only.

Ownership and communication:
- Release owner: The engineer listed on the release ticket (must be a member of eng-infra). Responsible for coordinating canaries, paging oncall, and documenting outcome.
- SRE escalation: If automated rollback fails or the fleet degrades despite rollback, escalate to SRE lead and Eng infra manager.
- Postmortem: Any rollback that required manual intervention beyond the checklist must result in a blameless postmortem within 72 hours.

Examples and snippets:
- Example terraform snippet to pin image and module: 
  module "gpu_node_group" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//gpu-node?ref=v2.4.1"
    image_tag = "redwood/gpu-node:kg5-520-ctr1-q2-20250115-sha256-abc123"
    warm_pool_size = 8
    enable_gpu_isolation = true
  }

- Example kubectl command to check nodes by image tag:
  kubectl get nodes -L image-tag -o wide | grep kg5-520

Post-release evaluation checklist:
- Confirm 7d post-release telemetry shows no degradation across these metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, GPU utilization, OOM events, kernel oops frequency.
- Update internal compatibility catalog with lessons, and if necessary mark certain profiles as deprecated with migration guidance.

Appendices:
A) Common failure signatures and triage hints:
  - Symptom: widespread small (1–2%) error raises with p95 spike. Likely cause: userland runtime ABI mismatch or a missing libc.so dependency in the image. Triage: run container runtime strace on a failing pod, validate lib version.
  - Symptom: single-AZ GPU OOMs after upgrade. Likely cause: driver memory accounting change or quantized-kernel memory regression. Triage: incident runbook "gpu-hotpath-debug" and collect nvml samples.

B) Contacts and runbook links (internal):
  - eng-infra-release@redwood.example.com
  - SRE pager: #sre-oncall
  - Observability: #observability-team
  - Related docs: see related_pages metadata for pointers.

C) Change log (summary):
  - 2024-09-15: initial draft
  - 2024-11-30: added quant-profile promotion policy and telemetry gates
  - 2025-01-20: formalized Terraform lockfile requirement and updated rollback timing

If you are executing a release using this catalog and hit ambiguity, page the release owner listed on the ticket before taking destructive change. The goal is deterministic, reversible upgrades with explicit telemetry gates — not maximum speed.
